messages:
alice_support: FYI incoming escalation from a mid-market customer in us-west-2 — sudden p95/p99 jump on text-gen endpoints after last night's driver roll. Customer saw p95 ~120ms -> ~900ms and p99 spikes to ~2s. They provided a repro and traces. link: https://grafana.redwood/example/d/abc123/latency?orgId=1 :exclamation:

maya_eng-runtime: Thanks Alice. Can you paste the trace IDs and the model config? Any batching changes? Also pinging @raj_eng-infra and @john_storage.

alice_support: Trace IDs: trace-78910, trace-78911. Model: rwd-open-3b, serving variant: batch_size=8, max_tokens=512. No customer-side batching changes. They said the regression started ~2024-11-12 02:10 UTC (matches our infra rollout window).

raj_eng-infra: I pulled host metrics for the nodes serving that shard. iostat snapshot (host node-uw2-34):
```
Device            r/s     w/s   rkB/s   wkB/s  avgrq-sz avgqu-sz await r_await w_await  svctm  %util
nvme0n1         120.2   10.4  10240.0  256.0    85.6     12.4    9.1    1.1    8.0   0.40  96.5
```
avgqu-sz and %util are through the roof. Looks like IO wait causing host-side stalls and long tail.

john_storage: Also seeing NVME error bursts in dmesg on that host: `nvme nvme0: I/O 0 QID 3 timeout` repeated. Firmware version on that fleet is 2.1.7; there was a queued firmware from vendor but not rolled last week. I suspect driver/CUDA interaction increased IO amplification (big KV cache flushes).

maya_eng-runtime: If host IO stalls, the runtime's continuous-batching and KV cache writes will backpressure and inflate tail latency. Immediate mitigations we can do from the runtime side:
- Enable model fallback to smaller-quantized variant (rwd-open-3b-q8) for the affected customer routing policy
- Reduce max_batch_size to 1-2 for that shard to remove batching-induced bursts
- Temporarily disable async checkpoint flushes to reduce host write bursts

lina_eng-sre: Oncall plan:
1) Quarantine the worst nodes (node-uw2-34, node-uw2-35) from serving and let autoscaler spin up fresh instances in the pool.
2) Apply blkio throttling to limit write throughput on those nodes while we investigate: `echo "8:0 10485760" > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/docker/blkio.throttle.write_bps_device` (example)
3) If rollback window is open, schedule driver rollback on a small canary to validate.

tim_oncall: Rolling rollback will need a 30m maintenance window and CS notification. Customer is impacted but not yet at SLA breach; recommend performing runtime-side routing fallbacks first to reduce customer pain while infra teams triage. I'll notify CS. :phone:

alice_support: Sharing quick repro steps from customer to help reproduce internally:
1) POST /v1/generate with model=rwd-open-3b, batch=1, prompt ~300 tokens
2) Repeat requests at 10rps for ~60s
3) Observe p95/p99 increase in our traces (attached)

raj_eng-infra: Reproduction locally on a repro node shows same pattern. Captured kernel stack snippets and nvme-cli output: `nvme list && nvme get-feature /dev/nvme0 --feature-id=0x0D` returned intermittent timeouts. Suggest trying firmware bump to 2.1.9 on a canary or enabling NVMe arbitration changes (vendor doc).

john_storage: Filed STORAGE-3421 for firmware canary. In the short term I can throttle background GC and host-side flushes. Also adding kernel tunable: `echo 300 > /sys/module/nvme_core/parameters/admin_timeout` to reduce noisy retries (we'll keep conservative).

maya_eng-runtime: I'll push a routing policy change to move the customer to q8 variant + set max_batch_size=2 for their tenant id. Also enabling prefix-KV warmup to avoid cold flush storms. Deploying now.

infra-bot: deploy-service: routing-policy updated for tenant=acme-corp by maya_eng-runtime at 2024-11-12T03:40:12Z

lina_eng-sre: After routing change, customer reports immediate improvement in p95 (~140ms). p99 still elevated but much reduced. Next steps: coordinate firmware canary, monitor tail, decide on driver rollback if firmware can't land.

tim_oncall: I'll coordinate the maintenance window and update the incident ticket. Thanks everyone for quick triage.

alice_support: Customer update sent: we've applied routing fallback and are working on infra mitigations. Will keep them updated every 30m. :white_check_mark:

maya_eng-runtime: Follow-up action items:
- (maya) Revert lifestyle flags to default after firmware validated
- (raj) Run firmware canary on one host and report nvme error delta by EOD
- (john) Add temporary blkio throttles to 5 nodes as precaution
- (lina) Draft rollback plan for driver if firmware canary fails
- (tim) Coordinate CS comms and maintenance window

alice_support: Adding incident tag and linking to ticket INC-2024-871. Closing thread here, updates will be in the ticket and follow-up threads.

lina_eng-sre: small note: capture `perf sched` and `iostat -x 1` during canary to correlate.

maya_eng-runtime: Agreed — will snapshot runtime metrics and KV cache stats during canary.

john_storage: I'll also schedule a storage health scan across uw2 fleet overnight.

alice_support: Thanks all.
